pathway.title: DIEBOLD NIXDORF, Inc — Full credit assessment
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: - Revenue durability supports the credit, but the mix is moving the wrong way. Services were 56.99% of FY2025 revenue and no customer exceeds 10%, yet Banking sales fell 1.92% in nine months of 2026, product backlog fell 7.21% to USD 733.1 million at 2025-12-31, and the revenue outlook implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 1,053.3 million to USD 1,093.3 million, a change of -4.61% to -0.99% from USD 1,104.2 million a year earlier. Retail grew 21.88%, but its segment gross margin of 21.69% is below Banking's 27.45%, so Retail growth dilutes margin as Banking shrinks. Basis: calculation C3; calculation C11; calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Margins are the weakest dimension and earnings quality is slipping. Product gross margin was 22.2% in the third quarter against 27.3% a year earlier, selling and administrative expense rose 7.6% against revenue growth of 4.27% in nine months, and reported EBITDA for the quarter fell 36.12% to USD 66.5 million while adjusted EBITDA rose 4.84% to USD 127.8 million; the gap is items the issuer adds back, which make up 36.69% of its nine-month adjusted EBITDA. The company cut the midpoint of its adjusted EBITDA outlook by 4.31% to a range of USD 490 million to USD 510 million. Basis: calculation C5; calculation C10; calculation C15; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 6–7; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Cash conversion has broken in 2026 and the outlook depends on a seasonal rebound. Free cash flow was an outflow of USD 68.5 million in nine months and USD 127.2 million over the last twelve months, which converts 38.84% of EBITDA against 73.34% in FY2025, while inventories absorbed USD 51.1 million and deferred revenue fell 22.01%. The free cash flow outlook of USD 190 million to USD 210 million was cut 23.81% at its midpoint and needs USD 226.2 million to USD 246.2 million in the fourth quarter, which is 15.59% to 25.80% above the USD 195.7 million of a year earlier, and the company expects to be a cash taxpayer in Germany from now on. Basis: calculation C1; calculation C2; calculation C5; calculation C8; calculation C12; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 2; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Financial policy is the swing factor, and it is discretionary. Treasury share activity of USD 154.9 million was 72.65% of the USD 213.2 million rise in net debt over nine months of 2026, the board approved a further USD 250.0 million programme on 2026-10-28, and net debt of USD 764.4 million, or USD 783.7 million pro forma for repurchases through 2026-10-23, puts net leverage at 2.33x, or 2.39x pro forma, against 1.69x at year-end 2025. Basis: calculation C6; calculation C7; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Leverage and coverage are moderate and are not the immediate problem. Total debt to reported EBITDA is 2.90x, EBITDA covers cash interest 4.27x over the last twelve months and covers the USD 73.6 million of contractual interest on the 2030 notes 4.45x, so the structure can absorb a weak quarter; the pressure is the direction of net leverage rather than its level. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C9; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 19; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Refinancing capacity is adequate because nothing falls due before the revolver matures on 2029-12-18, three months before the 2030 notes mature on 2030-03-31. Interest expense fell 44.8% after the December 2024 refinancing, all three rating agencies hold stable outlooks after 2025 upgrades by Moody's and S&P, and the revolver was undrawn at 2026-09-30, but the notes and the revolver share the same first-priority liens, so a later refinancing has no unencumbered collateral to offer a new class of creditors. Basis: calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 9; Business & governance (CP-1A); Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Liquidity is adequate but shrinking. Cash plus the undrawn revolver was USD 470.7 million at 2026-09-30 against USD 673.0 million at year-end 2025, a fall of 30.06%, and liquidity pro forma for the repurchases through 2026-10-23 is not established. Basis: calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1)

- Governance and financial policy are medium risk and cap the credit view. Two holders own 46.9% of the shares, the share count fell 10.66% in 20 months, and the covenant limits on repurchases are not established, so the willingness to return cash is documented but the capacity to do so is not bounded. Basis: calculation C13; Business & governance (CP-1A)

- The primary downside path runs from a fourth-quarter cash shortfall through continued buybacks to a thinner liquidity cushion and higher net leverage, with product margin as the first operating break. If fourth-quarter free cash flow falls short of USD 226.2 million while repurchases continue under the new programme, net debt rises again from USD 764.4 million, or USD 783.7 million pro forma, and liquidity falls below the USD 470.7 million of 2026-09-30, a figure that is before the repurchases through 2026-10-23 and has no pro forma; no maturity forces action before 2029-12-18, so the first result is erosion of the cushion rather than a default event. Basis: calculation C2; calculation C7; calculation C12; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

runs.text: The main credit supports are a services base that is 56.99% of revenue with no customer above 10%, a capital structure of one secured note and an undrawn revolver with nothing due before 2029-12-18, a 44.8% cut in interest expense after the 2024 refinancing, moderate total leverage of 2.90x with cash interest cover of 4.27x, and Retail growth of 21.88% that offsets the Banking decline. Basis: calculation C9; calculation C13; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

The main constraints are negative cash generation in 2026, discretionary buybacks that lifted net leverage to 2.33x, or 2.39x pro forma, from 1.69x, a third-quarter product gross margin of 22.2% against 27.3%, a product backlog that fell 7.21%, and an outlook cut that leaves the fourth quarter carrying the year's cash flow, while the limits that covenants place on repurchases are not established. Basis: calculation C7; calculation C13; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 7; Financial foundation (CP-1); Business & governance (CP-1A)

blocks.title: Transaction summary and new debt issues

runs.text: The only new debt issue in the sources is the refinancing of 2024-12-18, when the company issued USD 950.0 million of 7.75% senior secured notes due 2030 at par and entered into a USD 310.0 million revolver maturing 2029-12-18, using the proceeds with revolver borrowings and cash on hand to repurchase all Exit Facility term loans, repay the prior revolver and pay premiums, fees and expenses. No debt was issued in 2025 or in the first nine months of 2026, and the revolver was borrowed and repaid within the period for USD 37.0 million. A sources-and-uses table for the refinancing is not stated. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 17; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 78–80; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 56; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 12

Completed transactions after emergence are small: USD 24.5 million of investments in multi-vendor capabilities and premium services in North America and other strategic investments in 2025, and the September 2023 sale of the held-for-sale non-core European retail business. Shareholder-return programmes are larger: USD 100.0 million announced 2025-02-12 and completed in the fourth quarter of 2025, USD 200.0 million approved 2025-11-05 with USD 23.5 million left at 2026-09-30, and USD 250.0 million approved 2026-10-28. Basis: 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, pages 18–19; 10-K_2025-12-31_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 98; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 10; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 25

Announced or pending items carry no terms: the non-core Turkey operation is to be wound down by the end of 2026, the company is exploring strategic options for an unconsolidated Chinese subsidiary after a USD 16.9 million impairment, and a possible strategic collaboration with Euronet Worldwide, Inc. has no definitive agreement, price, funding or date. No purchase price, valuation, sponsor economics or pro forma leverage is stated for any transaction other than the refinancing, and none is estimated here. Basis: 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 4; 10-Q_2026-09-30_dbd.htm.jsonl, page 8; EX99.1_2026-09-30_dbd_ex-991q32026erlive-htm.htm.jsonl, page 14

fields.value: - Leverage is stable on year-end figures and rising on net debt. Total debt to reported EBITDA was 2.85x for FY2024, 2.88x for FY2025 and 2.90x on the last twelve months to 2026-09-30, while net debt rose by USD 213.2 million in nine months to USD 764.4 million as cash fell from USD 387.3 million to USD 184.9 million. The largest use of cash was treasury share purchases of USD 154.9 million, followed by free cash outflow of USD 68.5 million (an operating cash outflow of USD 29.3 million plus capital spending and capitalised software of USD 39.2 million). Last-twelve-month EBITDA did not fall, so the rise in net leverage comes mainly from the discretionary buyback. A further USD 19.3 million of shares was bought after quarter-end and the board approved a new USD 250.0 million programme on 2026-10-28, which points to a further rise. Pro forma for those purchases net debt is USD 783.7 million and net leverage 2.39x.

fields.value: - Cash generation turned negative in 2026 and the customer-prepayment float is shrinking. Deferred revenue, a non-interest-bearing funding source, fell by USD 71.7 million to USD 254.1 million, so customers are funding less of the business. Free cash flow was an outflow of USD 68.5 million for nine months against USD 43.3 million of inflow, and last-twelve-month free cash flow converts only 38.84% of EBITDA against 73.34% in FY2025.

fields.value: The strongest case against concern is that the weakness is seasonal and discretionary. Fourth-quarter 2025 operating cash flow, found as the year less nine months, was USD 217.5 million, 72.33% of the year's inflow, and the nine-month 2026 outflow includes USD 32.3 million of discrete German tax payments for earlier years and an inventory build that the quarterly report attributes to higher memory costs, finished goods and seasonality; the buyback is the largest use of cash and the board may suspend it at any time. The view would soften if fourth-quarter 2026 operating cash flow approaches the fourth-quarter 2025 level and buybacks stay within the authorisation already in use, and it would harden if cash falls further while repurchases continue under the new USD 250.0 million programme.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Diebold Nixdorf is a scaled, services-led self-service technology supplier with no named sponsor, so creditor risk lies in discretionary shareholder returns and thinning product margins rather than buyout leverage; governance risk is medium because covenant limits and legacy litigation status are not established.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Services are 56.99% of revenue and no customer exceeds 10%, which supports cash-flow visibility, but product backlog fell 7.21% in 2025 and Banking sales are shrinking while Retail grows. Funds associated with two holders own 46.9% of the stock, and share repurchases of USD 148.6 million in nine months of 2026 ran ahead of free cash flow, which was an outflow of USD 68.5 million.

The only order measure stated in amounts, product backlog, was USD 733.1 million at 2025-12-31 against USD 790.1 million a year earlier, so hardware demand was lower entering 2026.

The view would soften if fourth-quarter 2026 cash flow rebuilds the cash used in nine months and the covenant documents show tight limits on restricted payments, and it would harden if repurchases continue under the new USD 250.0 million authorisation while free cash flow stays negative, if an appraisal ruling adds material compensation, or if the Euronet collaboration is financed with debt.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Diebold Nixdorf has an adequate but weakening credit profile: services-led revenue and a single 2030 maturity support creditors, but cash generation turned negative in 2026 and buybacks lifted net leverage, so credit quality now depends on a fourth-quarter cash rebuild.

Reaching the full-year outlook needs fourth-quarter free cash flow of USD 226.2 million to USD 246.2 million on the company's definition, against USD 195.7 million a year earlier.

fields.value: - Revenue durability supports the credit, but the mix is moving the wrong way. Services were 56.99% of FY2025 revenue and no customer exceeds 10%, yet Banking sales fell 1.92% in nine months of 2026, product backlog fell 7.21% to USD 733.1 million at 2025-12-31, and the revenue outlook implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 1,053.3 million to USD 1,093.3 million, a change of -4.61% to -0.99% from USD 1,104.2 million a year earlier. Retail grew 21.88%, but its segment gross margin of 21.69% is below Banking's 27.45%, so Retail growth dilutes margin as Banking shrinks.

fields.value: - Margins are the weakest dimension and earnings quality is slipping. Product gross margin was 22.2% in the third quarter against 27.3% a year earlier, selling and administrative expense rose 7.6% against revenue growth of 4.27% in nine months, and reported EBITDA for the quarter fell 36.12% to USD 66.5 million while adjusted EBITDA rose 4.84% to USD 127.8 million; the gap is items the issuer adds back, which make up 36.69% of its nine-month adjusted EBITDA. The company cut the midpoint of its adjusted EBITDA outlook by 4.31% to a range of USD 490 million to USD 510 million.

The free cash flow outlook of USD 190 million to USD 210 million was cut 23.81% at its midpoint and needs USD 226.2 million to USD 246.2 million in the fourth quarter, which is 15.59% to 25.80% above the USD 195.7 million of a year earlier, and the company expects to be a cash taxpayer in Germany from now on.

fields.value: The strongest evidence against a weakening view is that the 2026 weakness is seasonal and discretionary. The view would soften if fourth-quarter free cash flow reaches USD 226.2 million and repurchases pause, and it would harden if free cash flow falls short while repurchases continue, if product gross margin stays at or below the 22.2% of the third quarter, or if the next outlook cuts adjusted EBITDA again.

fields.value: Diebold Nixdorf makes and services ATMs, cash recyclers, point-of-sale and self-checkout systems with software for banks and retailers worldwide. Services were 56.99% of FY2025 revenue of USD 3,805.7 million, Banking was 73.50% and Retail 26.50%, EMEA was 53.91% by point of origin, and no customer exceeds 10%, so cash flow rests on a large installed base serviced under maintenance and managed-service contracts whose tenor is not stated. Hardware refresh cycles at banks drive the product half of the business, which is why backlog and Banking product sales matter more to the credit than the services share alone.

fields.value: The company is listed and has no sponsor. Funds associated with two holders own 46.9% between them, the share count fell 10.66% in 20 months, and the filings document repurchases but no related-party dealings or control rights. The 2024 refinancing left one secured note and one revolver that rank equally under first-priority liens on substantially all assets, with guarantees from subsidiaries whose names were not supplied, so creditors share one collateral pool and are exposed to the same shareholder-return decisions.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Revenue is part recurring and part cyclical. Services grew 3.69% in nine months of 2026 and give visibility, while product revenue depends on bank and retailer refresh cycles; product backlog was USD 733.1 million at 2025-12-31 against USD 790.1 million a year earlier, and tariff recoveries of USD 10.0 million and pricing actions show partial pass-through of cost increases. Revenue is therefore predictable in services, cyclical in Banking products and growing but lower-margin in Retail, with limited pricing power in hardware where large competitors are named.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Margins are exposed to component prices and overhead growth. The principal raw materials are steel, plastics and electronic parts bought from major suppliers, memory costs were elevated in 2026, selling and administrative expense grew 7.6% against revenue growth of 4.27%, and the restructuring programme has recognised USD 105.1 million of an expected USD 125 million, mainly for headcount, with savings not quantified. Operating leverage is therefore negative today, and margins can be defended only if the programme's savings arrive while product margins stay low.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Capital intensity is low and cash conversion is volatile. Capital expenditure and capitalised software were USD 37.4 million and USD 24.3 million in FY2025, and USD 19.0 million and USD 20.2 million in nine months of 2026; FY2025 free cash flow of USD 239.0 million converted 73.34% of EBITDA, but nine-month 2026 free cash flow was an outflow of USD 68.5 million as inventories absorbed USD 51.1 million, deferred revenue fell 22.01% and discrete German tax payments took USD 32.3 million. Capital spending is modest against EBITDA, so conversion depends mainly on working capital and taxes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Competitive rivalry is high in hardware, where the annual report names NCR Atleos, Hyosung TNS and Hitachi Channel Solutions among Banking competitors and NCR Voyix and Toshiba among Retail competitors, and it is fragmented in services, where local and regional providers compete. Buyer power is likely high because banks and large retailers buy in volume, although no customer above 10% limits single-customer loss; supplier power is material for memory and electronic parts, whose elevated cost cut product margin; the threat of substitutes comes from payment options other than cash, which the company itself cites as a risk to ATM usage; and the threat of new entrants is not established from the sources.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: External factors are material in three places. Tariffs and trade policy are cited risks and USD 10.0 million of tariff recoveries and pricing actions only partly offset the margin decline, the euro and German exposure matter because EMEA is 53.91% of revenue and Germany is 19.03%, and the German cash taxpayer position adds a recurring tax outflow that free cash flow did not carry before. The social and technological factor that matters most is the shift away from cash, which could reduce ATM usage over the life of the 2030 notes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: In credit terms the strengths are the services base, the customer spread, the refinanced structure and Retail momentum; the weaknesses are product margin, volatile cash conversion, discretionary buybacks and overhead growth; the opportunities that could improve credit quality are restructuring savings and large cash-recycler and self-checkout contract wins reported for the third quarter; and the threats are lower cash use, memory and tariff costs, and German cash taxes.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: On the nine financial-profile dimensions the assessments are as follows. Scale and market position is average, with revenue of USD 3,805.7 million but no peer data. Competitive advantage is average and rests on the serviced installed base. Business diversification is average, balanced between Banking and Retail and across regions but with Banking at 73.50% of revenue. Cost and capex flexibility is average, because capital spending is modest but overhead is rising. Margin stability is weak, with product gross margin at 22.2% in the third quarter against 27.3%. Free cash flow stability is weak, swinging from USD 239.0 million in FY2025 to an outflow of USD 68.5 million in nine months of 2026. Ability to refinance and access capital markets is average, with nothing due before 2029-12-18 but ratings from single-B to BB- and a fully secured structure. Liquidity position is average at USD 470.7 million before the repurchases through 2026-10-23, and falling. Financial policy and governance is average, held back by repurchases above free cash flow and unbounded covenant limits. The trend is negative, and the missing data are fourth-quarter results, the debt documents and peer comparisons.

fields.value: Over the next year or two the company's own outlook is the reference point, and its full-year range implies fourth-quarter revenue of USD 1,053.3 million to USD 1,093.3 million, adjusted EBITDA of USD 142.5 million to USD 162.5 million and free cash flow of USD 226.2 million to USD 246.2 million; that is a change of -4.61% to -0.99% in revenue from a year earlier but 11.50% to 27.15% above the third quarter in adjusted EBITDA, so the plan relies on cost savings and seasonality rather than growth. Tailwinds are Retail wins, cash-recycler and branch-automation contracts and restructuring savings that are not yet quantified; headwinds are memory and tariff costs, German cash taxes and the lower backlog. Over the longer term the 2029 revolver and 2030 notes will need refinancing from a business whose Banking hardware demand faces structurally lower cash use, so cash discipline now determines refinancing terms later.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The downside scenario is specific to this issuer. The initiating condition is weaker Banking hardware demand and product margins staying at the third-quarter level of 22.2%, so fourth-quarter revenue lands at the low end of the implied range of USD 1,053.3 million and adjusted EBITDA below the USD 490 million floor. The first operating break is cash conversion: free cash flow falls short of the USD 226.2 million that the outlook needs and net debt stays near USD 764.4 million, or USD 783.7 million pro forma, instead of reversing. The financial transmission is that repurchases under the new USD 250.0 million programme would be paid from a liquidity cushion that was USD 470.7 million at 2026-09-30, before the repurchases through 2026-10-23, and net leverage would move further above 2.33x, or 2.39x pro forma. Management can suspend repurchases, cut capital spending and draw on the revolver, so liquidity distress is unlikely before the 2029-12-18 revolver maturity; the realistic outcome is a weaker rating trajectory and a harder refinancing in 2029, not a default.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Overall, Diebold Nixdorf presents an adequate business profile supported by a large services base, a customer spread with no customer above 10% and a refinanced structure, but credit quality is constrained by negative 2026 cash generation, discretionary buybacks and thin product margins. Cash-flow durability appears adequate in services and weak in products. Refinancing capacity is likely to depend on the fourth-quarter cash rebuild, the pace of repurchases and a stable ratings trend ahead of the 2029-12-18 revolver and 2030-03-31 note maturities. The primary downside path is a fourth-quarter cash shortfall with continued repurchases. Further analysis would require the executed debt documents, the proxy statement, fourth-quarter results and peer data. Top risk: shareholder returns that exceed free cash flow.
